newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM says EU vetting of Finnpap routine.
newsitem.headline: UPM says EU vetting of Finnpap routine.

text.p: Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Wednesday that a European Commission vetting of its acquisition of the Finnpap marketing association would be a routine measure.

"The examination of UPM-Kymmene's Finnpap deal announced by the EU Commission is a normal routine measure linked to the final formal stage of the dismantling of the marketing association," UPM-Kymmene said in a statement.

In practice, any barriers to the merger of Finnpap with UPM-Kymmene had been removed already when EU competition authorities permitted the 1996 merger of Kymmene Oy and Repola Oy which created UPM-Kymmene, and the requirement to end joint sales operations was fulfilled last year, UPM said.
The European Commission said on Tuesday it had started a routine review of the deal under which UPM-Kymmene takes control of Finnpap as announced in January 1997.
The Commission has one month to complete its investigation and either clear the deal or start a detailed, four-month inquiry. Most deals are approved after one month.

UPM-Kymmene said in December that the joint activities of Finnpap would be wound up at the end of 1996 and that Finnpap's corporate format would be changed into a joint stock company, after which UPM would buy the other partners' stakes.
The other partners in Finnpap, founded in 1918, were Metsa-Serla and Myllykoski Oy.
